# Elite-style Space Trading and Combat Game - Brief

## Problem Statement

The initiative aims to create a single-player space trading and combat game inspired by the classic Elite. The problem being addressed is the need for an engaging browser-based game that combines economic trading mechanics with arcade-style combat, running entirely locally without external dependencies.

## Objective

Create a self-contained, offline-capable web application that delivers a complete single-player space trading and combat experience playable immediately after installation via `npm install && npm start`, with no manual build steps required.

## Actors

- **Player**: Single user who starts docked at a station with 100 credits and a small cargo hold
- **Developer**: Person who will implement and maintain the game codebase
- **Quality Assurance**: Will validate unit tests, browser smoke tests, and /healthz endpoint

## Scope

### In Scope

- Node.js server serving a single HTML/JS frontend
- Canvas/WebGL rendering system with parallax starfield
- At least 8 named star systems with stations
- Commodity market with dynamic per-system pricing
- Hyperspace jump mechanics with fuel consumption and pirate encounter probability
- Ship-to-ship combat with player lasers vs enemy AI
- Ship upgrades (cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank)
- Save/load game state functionality
- Unit tests for core mechanics
- Browser smoke test
- /healthz endpoint on the server

### Explicit Non-Scope

- Multiplayer functionality
- External CDN dependencies
- Cloud-based save/load
- WebSocket or real-time communication
- Mobile browser support (Chrome desktop focus)
- In-game purchases or monetization
- Network-based features or APIs

## Constraints

### Technical Constraints

- Single-player only (no real-time communication required)
- Chrome browser as primary target
- 60fps target on 2020 laptop hardware
- Fully offline (no external CDN dependencies)
- English UI only
- Local filesystem access for save/load is acceptable

### Development Constraints

- Node.js development environment required
- No manual build steps for running the game
- Server must expose /healthz endpoint
- Unit tests required for core mechanics
- Browser smoke test required

## Assumptions

- Node.js is available on the development machine
- Chrome is the target browser and will be used for testing
- The player has basic familiarity with space trading games
- A 2020 laptop is a reasonable minimum hardware target for 60fps
- WebSocket or similar real-time communication is not required (single-player)
- Local filesystem access for save/load is acceptable

## Unknowns

- Exact pricing algorithms for commodity market dynamics
- Specific combat balance and enemy AI behavior parameters
- Precise visual effects implementation details (particle systems, shaders)
- Optimal canvas/WebGL rendering approach for the target hardware
- Exact save/load format and storage mechanism (localStorage vs files)

## Complexity Profile

- **Complexity Rating**: XS
- **Topology Hint**: Sequence (linear game progression with branching decisions)
- **Shared Mutation Risk**: false (single-player, no concurrent state)
- **Rationale**: The initiative is well-scoped for an XS complexity web-app with clear functional and non-functional requirements. The gameplay mechanics are classic and well-understood, reducing design uncertainty. The technical stack (Node.js + canvas/WebGL) is mature and capable of delivering the required experience.

## Constraints

- ord-c-001 (open-question): Exact pricing algorithms for commodity market dynamics
- ord-c-002 (open-question): Specific combat balance and enemy AI behavior parameters
- ord-c-003 (open-question): Precise visual effects implementation details (particle systems, shaders)
- ord-c-004 (open-question): Optimal canvas/WebGL rendering approach for the target hardware
- ord-c-005 (open-question): Exact save/load format and storage mechanism (localStorage vs files)
- ord-c-006 (synthesis): the delivered product is synthesized and assembled as one whole that is runnable locally
- ord-c-007 (ordered-smoke): an ordered smoke test performs the install step, then the start step, then reaches the running product

## Constraints Dispositions

All open-question constraints are deferred to the development phase where they will be resolved through implementation and testing:
- ord-c-001: Deferred - Pricing algorithms will be determined during development based on gameplay balance testing
- ord-c-002: Deferred - Combat balance parameters will be tuned during development through playtesting
- ord-c-003: Deferred - Visual effects implementation will be chosen during development based on performance testing
- ord-c-004: Deferred - Rendering approach will be optimized during development for target hardware
- ord-c-005: Deferred - Save/load mechanism will be selected during development based on technical requirements
- ord-c-006: Accepted - The product will be delivered as a complete, runnable local application
- ord-c-007: Accepted - The product will include ordered smoke tests for install, start, and running validation
